BiblicalUsage: Onan was a son of Judah, named in the genealogy of the tribe and in the census of the wilderness. When his brother Er died, Judah told Onan to go in to his brother's wife and raise up seed to his brother, and Onan refused, and the thing he did displeased the Lord.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Onan's story is the warning against refusing the duty God lays on a man: he spilled his seed on the ground, and the Lord slew him.
